body: Dungeons & Dragons: Heroes is Atari's Xbox action role-playing game, first released in North America on 16 September 2003. Four adventurers are brought back to life to face Kaedin, the wizard whose final spell killed them after their earlier victory. A dwarf cleric, elf wizard, halfling rogue and human fighter supply the party's different roles. The player travels through a campaign built around fighting, equipment and character development, either alone or with companions. The tabletop setting provides creatures and fantasy identities for an adventure designed around immediate, shared console action.

Up to four players can join or leave during play, and characters of different levels can travel together. Each class brings its own abilities to the group, while levelling supplies points and skills that can be assigned after the immediate fight is over. The system keeps character development connected to the action without demanding a pause in the middle of every encounter. Familiar Dungeons & Dragons monsters give the party a recognisable sequence of threats. Cooperation grows from making the available roles useful together as the group crosses another room or confronts a stronger enemy.

The campaign sends the revived heroes after Planar Gems tied to different planes of existence, giving the journey a structure of exploration and recovered power. Four difficulty levels extend the challenge, with Nightmare becoming available after completing Hard. Gary Spinrad composed the score, and Glenn Fabry supplied the cover artwork. Heroes uses the Dungeons & Dragons name to support an accessible action adventure rather than reproduce the full tabletop rules. Its central pleasure is the continuity of the party, allowing friends to enter the expedition, develop their characters and keep moving through the same fantasy world together.
